Name: belief_introspection_gap
Title: Acted vs. Avowed: Measuring the Gap Between an LLM's Operative Belief and Its Introspective Belief Report
Short Hypothesis: An LLM has two potentially divergent belief representations about a specific item: an *operative belief* that actually governs its task behavior, and an *avowed belief* it produces when asked to introspect ('Do you believe X?'). We hypothesize that (a) these are encoded along partially separable directions that can dissociate, (b) belief-vs-fact/knowledge errors and unfaithful self-reports arise when the avowed-belief pathway is decoupled from the operative-belief pathway, and (c) the introspection gap is causally reducible by steering the avowed-belief readout toward the operative-belief representation, improving self-report faithfulness without harming task behavior.
Related Work: Recent introspection work (Song et al. 2025 'Privileged Self-Access'; Martorell 2026 'Quantitative Introspection') studies whether LLM self-reports track internal temperature or emotive states, and hallucination-probing work (Ji et al. 2024; Wang 2026 'Confidently Wrong') shows internal states predict answer correctness better than verbalized self-assessment. The referenced 'Language models cannot reliably distinguish belief from knowledge and fact' and Suzgun et al. (KaBLE) show behavioral belief/knowledge/fact conflation. However, NONE isolate the specific dissociation between the belief that *drives an LLM's task action* (operative belief) and the belief it *reports when introspecting* (avowed belief) about a specific item, nor test whether unfaithful/self-contradictory belief reports arise from a decoupling of these two internal pathways, nor provide a causal steering fix that aligns the introspective readout to the operative representation. My prior proposals covered agent-attribution, update inertia, item-truth binding, temporal indexing, provenance, graded strength, and logical coherence; this operative-vs-avowed distinction is a new lens on belief self-report faithfulness.
Abstract: When an LLM answers a question it relies on some internal belief about the relevant facts; when we instead ask it 'Do you believe X?', it produces a self-report of that belief. Are these the same belief? We argue that an LLM may hold an *operative belief* that governs its task behavior while producing a distinct *avowed belief* under introspection, and that this gap underlies unfaithful self-reports and belief-vs-fact confusion. Using controlled items where we can measure both what the model acts on (its answer/choice on a task) and what it says it believes (an introspective query), we probe residual-stream activations of several open-weight models. We train probes to recover the operative belief (from the task-answer computation) and the avowed belief (from the introspection query) and measure their subspace alignment. We find (1) the two beliefs are decodable along partially separable directions and measurably dissociate on a subset of items; (2) large operative-avowed gaps predict behavioral self-report unfaithfulness (the model asserts believing something it does not act on, or vice versa) better than a confidence baseline; and (3) causally steering the avowed-belief readout toward the operative-belief representation reduces the introspection gap and improves self-report faithfulness without degrading task accuracy, whereas the reverse steer induces confident false self-reports. We introduce an introspection-gap metric and localize where the two pathways diverge across layers. This reframes belief-vs-fact confusion as an operative-vs-avowed dissociation and provides a cheap, interpretable intervention. All experiments run on <=9B open-weight models.
Experiments: 1) Dataset & paired-elicitation construction: Assemble items with a clear operative measurement and a matched introspective measurement. OPERATIVE: the model must use belief in P to complete a task (e.g., a multiple-choice QA, a bet/decision under a rule like 'act as if only true statements matter', or a downstream inference that only succeeds if P is/ isn't believed). AVOWED: a direct introspective query ('Do you believe P is true? Yes/No', 'How would you complete: I believe that P is ___'). Use factual (TriviaQA/PopQA/MMLU with per-item empirical accuracy) and neutral/fictional items to separate parametric priors from context. Include cases designed to induce dissociation: sycophantic pressure, distractor context, and hedging prompts. ~3k paired items with paraphrase/order randomization and single-condition controls. 2) Behavioral gap analysis: For each item, record the operative belief (inferred from the task choice) and the avowed belief (from introspection). Define behavioral introspection-gap-rate = fraction where avowed disagrees with operative. Measure how it scales with pressure/distractor/hedging conditions and factual-vs-fictional content; compare across first- vs third-person framings. Models: Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, plus a base-vs-chat pair. 3) Internal geometry: Extract residual-stream activations at (a) the operative task-answer position and (b) the introspection-query position. Train linear/logistic probes for the operative belief and the avowed belief. Report per-layer probe accuracy and subspace alignment (cosine / principal angles) between the operative-belief and avowed-belief directions; localize the layers where the two pathways diverge. 4) Error-geometry link: Test whether the internal operative-avowed alignment (or a decoded internal-gap score) predicts behavioral self-report unfaithfulness (AUC) beyond a verbalized-confidence baseline and beyond the model's own P(True). 5) Causal steering (double dissociation): Recover an 'alignment' direction via difference-of-means between aligned vs. dissociated item pairs. (a) Steer the avowed-readout toward the operative representation and measure whether the self-report flips to match the operative belief (controllability) while task accuracy is preserved (specificity). (b) Reverse steer to induce confident false self-reports, verifying the mechanism. Also validate with activation patching from the operative position into the introspection position. 6) Lightweight faithfulness fix: A small LoRA (or steering-only) with an auxiliary loss that increases operative-avowed alignment; evaluate introspection-gap-rate reduction, self-report faithfulness, retained task/factual accuracy (MMLU/TriviaQA subset), and calibration (ECE) of the improved self-reports. Metrics: introspection-gap-rate, operative-avowed subspace alignment, per-layer divergence localization, probe accuracy, prediction AUC vs. baselines, steering controllability & specificity, self-report faithfulness, retained accuracy, ECE.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The operative belief must be cleanly inferred from behavior; task design confounds (task difficulty, format) could contaminate the operative readout — mitigated by multiple operative task formats and controls where operative and avowed should trivially agree. 2) Stated avowed belief may reflect surface style rather than an internal readout; mitigated by pairing with the avowed probe. 3) Operative and avowed subspaces may not separate linearly; we also try MLP probes and report negatives as informative. 4) Apparent gaps could be noise/sampling variance; we estimate operative belief via repeated sampling and report confidence intervals. 5) Steering may have off-target effects; specificity/retention metrics quantify this. 6) Effects may vary across model families, elicitation formats, and scale; we report per-condition results rather than universal claims.
